content.en: Distinguish the student’s question from the adviser’s confirmed information. Check numbers and course names on replay.

strategies.vi: Làm bài trước khi xem đáp án; ghi lại câu chưa chắc và giải thích vì sao đáp án đúng.
strategies.en: Attempt the task first, then explain why the supported answer is right.

passages.title: L-B
passages.text: At sixteen, students can continue in school or college or combine work with part-time study. University applications can contain up to five choices, and a conditional offer normally requires specified grades. After a lecture, students may attend a seminar. Assessment can include assignments and exams. Further routes include a PGCE in Education for school teaching, a Master of Arts, or a doctorate. Placements provide commercial experience, while careers fairs help students meet employers.

audios.title: University applications and study
audios.transcript:
Advisor: Have you looked at the U C A S application website?
Student: Yes. How many university choices can I add?
Advisor: Up to five choices. They can be different courses or universities. Some offers are conditional, which means you must meet the required grades.
Student: What is a normal university day like?
Advisor: A lecture often comes first. A smaller seminar can follow the lecture, where students discuss ideas. Assessment may include assignments as well as exams.

audios.title: Further study and work options
audios.transcript:
Student: I want to continue studying, but I am still choosing a direction.
Advisor: If you want to teach in a school, a P G C E in Education is one possible route after a degree. You could also apply for a Master of Arts course. A doctorate, such as a P H D, normally takes at least three years.
Student: I would like some experience outside university too.
Advisor: Then consider a placement. It can help you gain commercial experience. To find work and meet employers, visit a careers fair. You can compare several opportunities there before deciding.
